He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State Rams]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]] and [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]]. Tonje was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Tonje attended [[Omaha Central High School]] in [[Omaha, Nebraska]], where he played basketball. As a sophomore, Tonje averaged 1.6 points per game but improved to 13.6 points per game as a junior. He was the second leading scorer for the Omaha Central Eagles during his junior campaign and connected on 46 percent of his three-point attempts. As a senior, Tonje averaged a Nebraska Class A State best 23.8 points along with 6.1 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.4 assists per game. He led the Eagles to a 22–6 record and a runner-up finish at the state tournament. His 73 triples and 82 percent free throw accuracy were tops at Class A. He set his school's single-season scoring record as a senior and earned first-team All-State by USA Today and All-Class State All-Tournament team honors.{{cite during his freshman and sophomore seasons.{{cite web|url=https://thednvr.com/5-takeaways-david-roddy-stars-in-a-resilient-comeback-effort-from-colorado-state-in-the-paradise-jam/|title=5 takeaways: David Roddy stars in a resilient comeback effort from Colorado State in the Paradise Jam|website=thednvr.com|date=November 20, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje scored a then-career-high 31 points in the first game of his junior season against [[2021–22 Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Oral Roberts]].{{cite web|url=https://thednvr.com/john-tonje-dischon-thomas-stand-out-in-a-dominant-team-performance-by-the-rams/|title=John Tonje, Dischon Thomas stand out in a dominant team performance by the Rams|website=thednrv.com|date=November 10, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje was a key to the success being dubbed the [[sixth man]] that helped lead the Rams to an [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] and getting to the semifinals.{{cite web|url=https://thednvr.com/year-in-review-john-tonje-shined-as-colorado-states-sixth-man/|title=Year-in-review: John Tonje shined as Colorado State's sixth man|website=tdnvr.com|date=April 12, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje bounced back and forth between the bench and starting lineup throughout his junior season. He was a big part of the success of the [[2020–21 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|2020–21 Colorado State Rams team]] that had a program best 16–1 start to the season.{{cite web|url=https://csurams.com/news/2022/1/22/mens-basketball-csu-runs-record-to-program-best-15-1-with-73-53-win-at-air-force|title=CSU Runs Record to Program Best 15-1 With 73-53 Win At Air Force|website=csurams.com|date=January 22, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje and the Rams qualified for the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] as an at-large bid for the program's first time since 2013 finishing the season with a 25–6 record. The sixth-seeded Rams were upset by 11th-seeded [[2021–22 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]].{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2022/03/17/michigan-tops-colorado-state-to-begin-march-madness-2022/|title=Michigan storms back to top Colorado State as March Madness 2022 begins|website=nypost.com|date=March 17, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2024|last=Cannizzaro|first=Mark}} Tonje became a full-time starter for the first time during his senior season. He posted career-per-game highs in points (14.6), rebounds (4.7), assists (1.3), steals (0.8) and blocks (0.3). Tonje decided to enter the [[transfer portal]] after his fourth season due to the extra year of eligibility from to the [[COVID-19]] season rule.{{cite web|url=https://milehighsports.com/csu-basketball-updates-john-tonje-enters-transfer-portal-mckenna-hofschild-will-be-back/|title=CSU Basketball updates: John Tonje enters transfer portal, McKenna Hofschild will be back|website=nypost.com|date=March 22, 2023|access-date=November 16, 2024}} ===Missouri=== Tonje decided to transfer to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]].{{cite web|url=https://missouri.rivals.com/news/summer-sessions-john-tonje|title=Summer Sessions: John Tonje|website=missouri.rivals.com|date=July 24, 2023|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje only appeared in eight games with the Tigers due to a season-ending foot injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.columbiatribune.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2024/01/16/mizzou-basketball-announces-john-tonje-will-miss-the-remainder-of-the-regular-season/72247947007/|title=Mizzou basketball announces John Tonje will miss the remainder of the regular season|date=2024-01-16|access-date=2026-08-11|last=Lewis|first=Jaden|publisher=Columbia Daily Tribune}} Tonje was granted a [[medical redshirt]] and a sixth year of eligibility. He then decided to enter the transfer portal for a second time.{{cite web|url=https://www.rockmnation.com/2024/4/15/24131262/report-john-tonje-set-to-enter-the-transfer-portal|title=REPORT: John Tonje set to enter the transfer portal|website=rockmnation.com|date=April 15, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}} ===Wisconsin=== Tonje was ranked as the 296th transfer portal player following the 2023–24 season.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/longformarticle/taking-stock-of-15-transfer-portal-ranking-misses-from-2024-aj-storr-johnell-davis-kobe-johnson-kanaan-carlyle-jonas-aidoo-aidan-mahaney-pj-haggerty--245264963/#2595027|title=Taking stock of 15 transfer portal ranking misses from the 2024 cycle|website=[[247Sports]]|date=February 6, 2025|access-date=March 15, 2025}} Tonje originally committed to [[Richard Pitino]] and [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]].{{cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/college/new-mexico-lobos/news/missouri-transfer-guard-john-tonje-commits-to-new-mexico/|title=Missouri transfer guard John Tonje commits to New Mexico|website=on3.com|date=April 25, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Less than a week later, Tonje decommitted from New Mexico and committed to Wisconsin.{{cite web|url=https://badgerswire.usatoday.com/2024/05/02/wisconsin-badgers-transfer-portal-commitment-john-tonje/|title=Wisconsin lands commitment from Missouri transfer guard John Tonje|website=baderswire.usatoday.com|date=May 2, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}} In only his fourth career game with the Badgers, Tonje scored a career-high 41 points in an upset victory over the ninth-ranked [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona Wildcats]]. His 41 points were the fourth most in a single game in Badgers history. Tonje also broke the Wisconsin single-game record for made free throws with 21.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/wisconsin-badgers-tonje-arizona-75307c6292b440692db1e8474caaa47e|title=Wisconsin guard John Tonje is wasting no time making his mark at his new shy of Frank Kaminsky's single-season scoring record|website=badgerswire.usatoday.com|date=March 23, 2025|access-date=March 23, 2025}} ==Professional career== ===Salt Lake City Stars (2025–2026)=== Tonje was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 53rd pick in the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Cox |first=Lorin |title=What Utah Jazz are getting in Wisconsin Badgers guard John Tonje |url=https://www.si.com/college/wisconsin/basketball/what-utah-jazz-are-getting-in-badgers-guard-john-tonje-scouting-report |access-date=July 4, 2025 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=July 4, 2025}} On August 26, 2025, Tonje signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Jazz. Under the terms of the deal, he would split time between the Jazz and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{cite news |title= Utah Jazz Sign John Tonje to Two-Way Contract |url= https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-john-tonje-to-two-way-contract |access-date=August 26, 2025 |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=August 26, 2025}} ===Boston Celtics (2026)=== On February 5, 2026, Tonje was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for center [[Chris Boucher (basketball)|Chris Boucher]] and a future second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-chris-boucher-and-a-future-second-round-draft-pick|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Chris Boucher and a Future Second-Round Draft the Celtics signed Tonje to a two-way contract.{{Cite web|title=Celtics' John Tonje: Staying in Boston on two-way deal|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-john-tonje-staying-in-boston-on-two-way-deal/|access-date=April 27, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en|date=March 1, 2026}} He ==Personal life== Tonje is the son of Sara and Jean. His father, Jean "Bertin" Tonje, is a native of [[Cameroon]] and played soccer for the [[Cameroon national football team]]. He has two brothers, Malcolm and Texan. He earned his bachelor's degree from Colorado State in Business/Real Estate and is currently studying Sports Leadership as a graduate student.{{cite web|url=https://uwbadgers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/john-tonje/13195|title=2024–25 Men's Basketball Roster John Tonje|access-date=November 16, 2024}} Tonje is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. He frequently mentions his faith on social media. He has said, "Sometimes it's hard to believe. Last night, I was reading an article about being All-American, which, I mean, doesn't even look right.
